scope: Comparative cross-national trust plus UK/US institutional performance and case evidence
dataUse: Cite primary source; no wholesale redistribution of controlled microdata. Check reuse restrictions before publishing transformed bulk data.
causality: None of these aggregate observations demonstrates that misconduct causes service failure or that either causes changes in trust.

observations.measure: Respondents with high/moderately high trust in national government
observations.population: OECD country respondents, not candidate country respondents
observations.note: Do not conflate with 43% low/no trust; remainder is neutral or uncertain.

observations.measure: Respondents with low/no trust in national government
observations.population: OECD country respondents
observations.note: Not the mathematical complement of high trust.

observations.measure: Believe people like them have a say in government decisions
observations.population: OECD country respondents
observations.note: Political agency, not a direct performance measure.

observations.measure: Trust gap by whether respondents report political voice
observations.population: OECD country respondents split by perceived political voice
observations.note: Descriptive association, not a causal treatment effect.

observations.measure: Trust gap for government-party supporters compared with others
observations.population: OECD survey respondents by reported governing-party support
observations.note: Observed gap; partisanship is a confounder.

observations.measure: Satisfied with administrative services among recent service users
observations.population: Respondents with recent administrative-service contact
observations.note: Not all respondents; not the national-government trust item.

observations.measure: Trust in national government
observations.population: UK ONS Trust in Government Survey respondents
observations.note: UK-specific experimental statistics.

observations.measure: Trust in civil service
observations.population: UK ONS Trust in Government Survey respondents
observations.note: Institution differs from national government.

observations.measure: Trust in NHS as public service
observations.population: UK ONS Trust in Government Survey respondents
observations.note: Trust in NHS, not satisfaction with current NHS performance.

observations.measure: Applications received by HM Passport Office January–September 2022
observations.population: HM Passport Office applications in period
observations.note: Approximately 7.2 million; not unique persons.

observations.measure: Customers receiving passports within published 10-week period
observations.population: Passport applicants in January–September 2022
observations.note: Approximately 95%, rounded.

observations.measure: Applicants experiencing waits longer than 10 weeks
observations.population: Passport applicants in January–September 2022
observations.note: Approximately 360,000. Not evidence of causation from political scandal.

observations.measure: IRS taxpayer correspondence inventory
observations.population: Correspondence pieces outstanding at fiscal year end
observations.note: Historic comparator; not equivalent to total unprocessed returns.

observations.measure: IRS taxpayer correspondence inventory
observations.population: Correspondence pieces outstanding at fiscal year end
observations.note: GAO cited year-end inventory.

observations.measure: IRS taxpayer correspondence inventory
observations.population: Correspondence pieces outstanding at fiscal year end
observations.note: Approximately 6.3 million; inventory includes different correspondence categories.

observations.measure: Late IRS taxpayer correspondence items
observations.population: Correspondence pieces outstanding at FY2025 end
observations.note: GAO reports 4.1 million / 65% late.

observations.measure: Share of taxpayer correspondence inventory overage
observations.population: IRS taxpayer correspondence inventory at fiscal year end
observations.note: Agency-reported GAO share; rounded, not derived from rounded totals.

observations.measure: Average paper return processing time
observations.population: IRS paper returns in 2024 filing season
observations.note: Different operation from correspondence processing.

observations.measure: Average paper return processing time
observations.population: IRS paper returns in 2025 filing season
observations.note: Shows improvement despite remaining backlog.

observations.measure: Share with lower WJP rule-of-law scores in 2025 than 2024
observations.population: Countries and jurisdictions in 2025 WJP index
observations.note: Not a measure of citizen trust; not an annual government-service metric.

events.subject: Boris Johnson
events.finding: House of Commons Privileges Committee concluded he deliberately misled the House and committed serious contempt.
events.disposition: Recommended 90-day suspension had he remained an MP; he had announced resignation before report publication.

events.subject: HM Passport Office
events.finding: Approximately 360,000 waited longer than ten weeks; about 95% received passports within ten weeks.
events.disposition: NAO investigation identified demand and processing-system and supplier constraints.

events.subject: Internal Revenue Service
events.finding: Correspondence backlog remained high, despite some improvements in paper return processing.
events.disposition: GAO recommended workforce and backlog planning.

researchQuestions.question: Does perceived elite impunity independently predict subsequent institutional trust, after controlling for political identity, economic conditions and prior trust?
Does directly experienced administrative burden independently predict trust in the delivering institution?
Is the interaction between perceived impunity and administrative burden superadditive in reducing trust?
Do transparency, sanctions, appeals and measured service improvements reduce or reverse any decline?
